submission.justification: CONDITIONAL RECOMMENDATION: the hard radiation-efficiency requirement is NOT verified. In the unirradiated simulation (100k events per point), Sensor-T2 gives the best single-hit resolution of the three technologies at every thickness. Its best value is 5.90 um at 125 um, and it stays within about 0.15 um of that from 100 to 175 um. Best values for the others: T3 9.3 um at 150 um; T1 13.8 um at 125 um. These agree with the 2025 summary. However, no project document and no available tool gives hit efficiency after irradiation, so it is unknown whether any candidate stays at or above 97% at 2e16 neq/cm^2. The simulation only covers unirradiated sensors. T2 at 125 um is therefore the best choice for resolution only. Before this choice is final, the collaboration must obtain irradiated test-beam or simulation efficiency data for T2 at about 125 um and 2e16 neq/cm^2. If T2 fails, the next options in resolution order are T3, then T1. T1 is a 3D-electrode sensor. That type is generally known in the field to be radiation hard, but nothing in this project's data confirms it. T1 would cost more than a factor of 2 in resolution (about 13.8 um).

requirements.requirement: Goal: best possible single-hit spatial resolution in the innermost layer
requirements.evidence: Unirradiated simulation scan from 50 to 300 um: best T2 is 5.90 um at 125 um, best T3 is 9.31 um at 150 um, best T1 is 13.76 um at 125 um. T2 at 125 um is the best point found.

requirements.requirement: Sensor must be one of the three technologies in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Sensor-T2 is listed in candidate_specs.md and is compatible with the readout chip according to readout_chip.md.

requirements.requirement: Hit efficiency at or above 97% up to 2e16 neq/cm^2 (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: No document (specs, meeting notes, readout chip, services, schedule, 2025 simulation summary) and no tool gives post-irradiation efficiency. The simulation is unirradiated only. This must be checked with irradiated data before the choice is final.
125 um is within the allowed range.

requirements.requirement: Submit one recommended technology and thickness
requirements.evidence: Sensor-T2 at 125 um submitted, conditional on the radiation-efficiency check.
